Text: 20 managers getting the same cost-cutting memo doesn’t mean the AI trade is dead. It means companies are figuring out which AI projects actually generate ROI instead of throwing money at every chatbot experiment. There’s a huge difference between a corporation pausing an overpriced AI pilot and hyperscalers abandoning AI infrastructure. AMD isn’t spending $8.2B on World Labs because it thinks another office assistant is the future. It’s targeting world models, physical AI, robotics, simulation, Instinct GPUs and ROCm, markets where AI actually has to interact with the real world. The first phase was “put AI in everything.” The next phase is prove it makes money. That shakeout doesn’t kill AMD’s opportunity. It concentrates the money into the companies that can actually deliver compute, software and useful applications. Bad AI projects dying ≠ AI dying. That’s called the market growing up. $AMD
